theme_note: The submitter presents the possible joke as breaking news; that initiating act is unlike the room's later testing and therefore stands alone.

second_order: testing and mocking the dating claim
theme_note: Commenters test the photograph and source, refuse belief, invoke Dispatch and the date, and joke about the identification; their replies vary from questions to mockery but all put the claim on trial.

second_order: enforcing standing post rules on joke and place submissions
theme_note: Moderators route or remove submissions using ordinary rumor, duplicate, body-text, and image rules; the rule varies while the shared practice is keeping event and joke posts inside standing posting boundaries.

second_order: working out what r/kpop should make and who will join
theme_note: Participants propose designs, ask for a vote, prefer group-neutral work, and test whether enough people will turn out; proposals vary, but each turn works on choosing a viable shared target.

second_order: building, correcting, and defending the Gee words
theme_note: Placers join the Gee effort, correct colours and accidental pixels, refresh before placing, add a border, and hold off overwriting; the tasks vary within the shared work of keeping the words on the canvas.

second_order: switching to fandom designs and swapping help
theme_note: When one target fails or needs help, participants move among the Seolhyun heart, f(x), and other fandom work, recruit named groups, alternate building and defense, and move some shared work into Discord.

second_order: arguing over territory and who attacked whom
theme_note: Neighbours and members dispute defacing, hearts, Robot Wars, and a Mauritian flag; positions range from refusing to return claimed space to saying r/kpop are the attackers and treating good relations as protection.

second_order: marking what survived, changed, or was lost
theme_note: Participants report takeovers and alterations, celebrate finished or surviving work, thank helpers, show results, and mourn a final gap; the outcome varies while the shared practice is accounting for what the canvas held.

second_order: playing an April Fools picture-clue game
theme_note: The room sets clue rules, posts and solves picture clues, hides answers, gives or declines hints, explains context, and jokes about moderator deletion; these are turns in one recurring game rather than canvas work.
A takeover proposal is met with questions, distance, calls for respect, an alternative location, humour, disbelief, and direct refusal; the replies differ but all contest replacing the existing flag.

second_order: asking for and locating a Korean flag on Place
theme_note: Across threads, posters request help for a Korean flag, clarify that Place means r/place, seek its location, and give landmarks; the requests range from starting to growing or relocating a flag.

second_order: asking about participation and disowning the post
theme_note: One title asks whether r/kpop will participate and the same account later attributes the post to a brother; missing text prevents making this a settled exchange, but both turns concern authorship of the participation question.

second_order: telling people to get off play-yan
theme_note: The surviving title is a hostile demand whose removed body leaves its target and circumstances unexplained, so it remains a single-code practice.
